title: General Terms and Exclusions Across the Travel Protection Plans
content:
Four general terms of the Travel Protection Plans are carried as a plain yes or no on each plan: whether
the insurer may recover a settled amount from a liable third party, whether illness arising from a declared
epidemic is covered rather than excluded, whether a terrorist incident at the destination is a covered
cancellation reason, and whether loss arising from war or civil unrest is excluded.

| Plan | Recovery from a liable third party applies | Epidemic illness covered | Terrorist incident covered | War and civil unrest excluded |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Trip Basics Essential | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Trip Basics Standard | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| TripGuard Plus | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| TripGuard Premier | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Cancel For Any Reason Elite | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Annual Multi-Trip Traveller | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Annual Multi-Trip Executive | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

## What the column of yeses and noes comes to

Recovery from a liable third party applies on all seven plans, and the exclusion of war and civil unrest stands
on all seven likewise. The two terms that divide the range are epidemic illness and terrorist incident: both are
excluded on Trip Basics Essential and Trip Basics Standard, and both are covered on TripGuard Plus, TripGuard
Premier, Cancel For Any Reason Elite, Annual Multi-Trip Traveller and Annual Multi-Trip Executive. No plan in
the range covers one of those two without the other.
